entries.text: For trade contractors who price their own jobs: a spreadsheet kit that works out labor, materials and overhead, then sets the price from your markup and shows the price that hits the margin you want.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: A 30% markup sounds safe until you see it is only about a 23% margin. Overhead that never gets spread over billable hours turns small jobs into losses, old material prices go stale, and the estimating still eats your evenings.
Before the quote goes out, you can see what the job really earns. After it is done, the Job Cost Tracker shows budget versus actual for each line, and the price book is better for the next one.
entries.note: No promise of winning jobs or earning more; describes what the kit shows.

entries.text: Enter your costs, your overhead and your markup, and the calculator gives the price.
entries.note: Check against the live calculator's actual inputs before shipping.

entries.text: Works out a year of overhead per billable hour, keeps your own price book of unit costs, and prints a client-ready quote. Includes a complete worked example to start from.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: Free templates are a fine start, and ours is free on this site. The kit adds what a blank template leaves to you: overhead recovery, markup pricing with a target-margin check, a price book and a Job Cost Tracker that shows budget versus actual for each line.
entries.note: Describes the product as the blueprint specifies it; G2 must check it against the delivered file before it ships.

entries.text: If you want scheduling, invoicing and a client portal, an app like those may suit you better. The kit is a one-time spreadsheet you own, focused only on getting the price right.
entries.note: Makes no claim about the apps' features or prices beyond the cited claim.

entries.text: The price book is yours: you enter your own unit costs and labor rates, so it fits your trade rather than a generic list. The worked example is an interior refresh (drywall and paint); change the lines to match your jobs.

entries.text: Open the kit and fill in the Overhead Calculator first: a year of overhead, your expected yearly job costs and your billable hours give the overhead % to use on every estimate and your overhead per billable hour.

entries.text: The kit does the arithmetic on the numbers you enter. Check licensing, permit, tax and contract rules for your trade and area yourself.
